[June 2032]

After years of R&D Greater West Africa and the Final Empire are ready to show off their new Helicopters. The demonstration event is at the Denel Overberg Test Range (DOTR) in the Western Cape.

Mike Kgobe, CEO of Denel Aviation, told DefenceWeb todays demonstration was aimed at talking to the broader community about the Rooivalk, with interested countries present at the demonstration, including delegations from Poland and Nigeria. Poland is currently seeking new attack helicopters under its Kruk programme while Nigeria has an urgent operational requirement for attack helicopters to combat Boko Haram militants.

Kgobe goes on to say, that today we have 3 new Rooivalks to demonstrate.

The Rooivalk Mk 2, which is the next generation Rooivalk and features better sights, improved firepower, greater payload, improved electronics and better survivability amongst other improvements, he said. The airframe and engines have been rebuilt using Metal foam but for the most part have stayed the same. The Mk 2 also has the capabiitlity to take direct control over the Rooivalk UCAV

The Rooivalk LA (Light Attack), is a Rooivalk made for the more cost minded and is built to compete with the Augusta A129 Mangusta unlike the Rooivalk Mk 1 & Mk 2 the RLA is built with Metal Foam,. a smaller frame (about the size of the A129) and is powered by a single Turbomeca Makila, and has a reduced payload. The LA does however have the improved electronics of the Mk 2.

The Rooivalk UCAV is for surveillance and reconnaissance. It is built using Metal Foam, a Fennec Frame and a single small Turbomeca Arriel. It packs enough of a payload in order to make a strategic strike or try to defend itself in air. It can be controlled from a control station, by a set of Power Armor Mk 4, or by the Rooivalk Mk 2
